proof_attempt_summary: First Omega(log T) minimax LOWER bound for adaptive superpopulation Horvitz-Thompson cumulative Neyman regret (resolving the open converse of Neopane-Ramdas-Singh 2024 / Noarov et al. 2025). The D0 math is complete and sound; the novel apparatus (kappa_nu curvature-information complexity, the tangent-regular class, the local->global lift, the recursion->log T accumulation) is fully machine-verified sorry-free. tldr: First matching-RATE minimax LOWER bound for superpopulation Horvitz-Thompson cumulative Neyman regret, resolving the open logarithmic converse: the O(log T) upper bounds of Neopane-Ramdas-Singh (2024) and Noarov et al. (2025) lacked a matching lower bound for this objective. The main theorem lower-bounds expected cumulative Neyman regret by a log T term times a closed-form local curvature-information complexity kappa_nu (S^2-scaled), and the global corollary gives an inf-sup Omega(log T) minimax rate on a named interior moment/overlap + strong-identification class. The universal RATE is log T; the fixed class radii control only the frontier CONSTANT K, whose closed-form moment envelope is solved here. The only remaining open object (OEQ) is the constant-sharp minimax value (a matching constant-sharp UPPER bound). This is the superpopulation Horvitz-Thompson converse, distinct from Chen-Ge-Qian-Harshaw's neighboring design-based AIPW upper/lower minimax program.
gap: The literature now has O(log T) upper bounds for adaptive Neyman regret and competitive analyses built around learning unknown arm standard deviations, but no matching lower bound for the same cumulative variance-regret objective. Nearby converses either target treatment-choice welfare regret or nonadaptive off-policy evaluation risk.
fill: The project fills that niche by turning second-moment learning delay into cumulative Neyman loss through bounded-outcome mean-preserving alternatives, producing both an instancewise complexity handle kappa_nu and a global Omega(log T) corollary on compact regular subclasses.
